result:
Round 36 passes on all six checks (R36-1 to R36-6), and the app was verified for real (`realVerified=true`). I changed no repository files; all my experiments ran in copies under `/tmp/c36`.

- **Files and frozen paths (R36-1):** only the 14 allowed files changed, and the only new file is `dom-queries.ts`. Both frozen-path checks exit 0, and no `getByRole("button"` call and no added timeout remain. Whether A wrote to `.claude/**` through Bash is unknown, because there is no transcript. A's result file shows no refused permissions.
- **Test changes (R36-2):** the only changed lines are the 24 lookups (same argument as before), the imports, the removed local helper, the (e5) rename and the new (b7)/(b8). All 11 imports sit in sorted position. Test counts are unchanged, except done-busy going from 6 to 8. The (b7)/(b8) bodies match my round 35 probes except for their names.
- **Mutants (R36-3):**
  - Each source mutant is caught by the tests the task names: SM-1, SM-2, DM-3, BM-1, DM-8 and BM-6.
  - DM-9 survives, as expected.
  - The old `3035ffc` source with A's tests fails as listed: (b1), (b2) and (b5) with the same symptoms as round 35, (b7) with `expected 'STALE1' to be 'B'`, and the (b4) unhandled rejection.
- **Speed (R36-4):** both runs on A's tree pass 289/289 in 18 files. The slowest test takes 402 ms, and (b1)–(b8) each take under 340 ms. The four target files are 7.5× to 14.2× faster. On this machine the slowest file took 15.6 s before (B measured 23 s), so the ratio holds even though the absolute numbers differ. Every component file also passes when run alone.
- **Gate and real app (R36-5):** the full gate exits 0, with the same 8 Biome warnings as round 35 and a clean typecheck that includes `dom-queries.ts`. Unit tests pass 289 renderer and 93 main. The real Electron app passes 7/7 E2E under xvfb, and 7/7 again with retries off. The app's source is unchanged from `46bd74b`.
- **Docs (R36-6):** `docs/bugs/001` has exactly the three requested text changes; the only new code reference is the `:227-228` the task asked for, and it points at the right lines. TESTING.md rule 6 is in the right place and nothing else in that file changed.

**One low finding (C-R36-01):** no test pins how the new helper matches buttons. Three changes to it all left the suite green: dropping the "more than one match" error, using substring matching, and removing the trim. On today's tests they make no difference. A probe over all 257 lookups showed each one finds exactly one button, the same one `getByRole` finds, so no test passes because the wrong button was picked. A small unit test for `dom-queries.ts` would close this.

Windows packaging was not checked: it is not available in the cloud and is not part of this round.
